...RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. MANJUNATH MALLAYYA SHETTY, ADVOCATE FOR R2,
 R1 IS SERVED)

THIS MFA IS FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.02.2024 IN MVC NO. 969/2022 PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT CHITTAPUR, AND BE PLEASED TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FRO RS.11,07,500/- TO RS. 14,50,000/- WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 12 PERCENT P.A, AND IMPOSE THE LIABILITY ON RESPONDENT NO.2 IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT

WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA) Though this matter has come up for admission,
with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for hearing.
2.
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 26.02.2024 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chittapur, in MVC No.969 of 2022.
3. The injured claimant, aged 46 years, doing agriculture, met with an accident on 01.02.2022, and filed NC: 2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR claim application claiming compensation of Rs.39,50,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted the compensation of Rs.11,07,500/- with interest at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till deposit,
and the Tribunal exonerated respondent No.2- insurance company from paying compensation and directed respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle to deposit the compensation amount.

4. Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant in which it is mainly contended that the monthly income of the claimant was wrongly taken as Rs.15,500/- and interest is to be enhanced.
The respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle was directed to pay compensation as the driver was not having the valid driving licence.

Therefore, it is contended that Basawaraj vs Ganapati And Anr on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117769933/
2 respondent No.2-insurance company may be directed to pay and recover.
Thus, requested for modification of the order.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent-insurance company contended that the liability was on the owner of the vehicle and he has have not filed any appeal.

As the claimant is NC: 2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR now asking for pay and recovery, the learned counsel is submitted that the amounts granted under the other heads are excessive and it is to be modified as per the law.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.
The injured claimant stated that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but he has not filed any income proof.
He met with an accident on 01.02.2022.

As per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.14,750/- per month and he was aged 46 years and the multiplier is to be taken as 13.
8.
The petitioner examined the doctor as P.W.2.

The doctor has stated that that petitioner was suffering from fracture of Zygomatic Arch, bilateral maxillary sinus and fracture of R- Orbit,
hemorrhagic contusion in P & O and frontal lobes.

In the wound certificate at Exhibit P3 it is stated that the petitioner has suffered the following injuries:
1. Head Injury.
2. Ear bleeding.
3. CLW of parietal region 5 X 3 cms 2 X 1 cms.
4. CLW over right frontal temporal 3 X 2 cms.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR 5.
Abrasion over Nose.
6. Multiple abrasion over left leg.
9. The doctor issued disability certificate as per Exhibit P8 and assessed the disability as 45% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has taken one third of 45% which comes to 15%.
Therefore, the disability needs no interference.

Thus, the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.3,45,150/-
(14,750x12x13x15%).
The petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 36 days.
He was admitted.
On 01.02.2022 and discharged on 08.03.2022 as per Exhibit P7.

Considering the nature of injuries,
period of hospitalisation and the other relevant factors, the amounts granted under the other heads including medical expenses at Rs.5,23,218/- needs no interference.
However, the loss of income during laid up period is to be modified as Rs.44,250/- (14,750 x 3) instead of Rs.46,500/-.

However,
the Tribunal granted Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses without any basis and therefore,
the claimant is not entitled for the said amount and it is to be deleted.

Therefore, the total Basawaraj vs Ganapati And Anr on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117769933/
3 compensation comes to Rs.10,37,618/-.

Thus, the compensation is reduced from NC:
2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR Rs.11,07,500/- to Rs.10,37,618/- with interest at 6% per annum.

10. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 3,45,150/-
 2.

Medical expenses 5,23,218/-
 3. Pain and Suffering 50,000/-
 4. Loss of amenities 50,000/-
 5. Transportation, extra 25,000/-
nourishment and attendant charges 6. Loss of earning during the laid up 44,250/-
 period
. The Tribunal observed that it is a case of no driving licence and fixed the liability on the owner of the vehicle.
Learned counsel for petitioner-claimant requested for pay and recovery by the respondent-insurance company.
Therefore, in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the NC: 2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR case of PAPPU AND OTHERS.

VS. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018)3 SCC 208, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that when there is no driving licence, the insurance company has to pay compensation and then, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle, the respondent-insurance company is directed to pay compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

12. In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The petitioner-claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.10,37,618/- with interest at 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation within one month from the date of this order.

Basawaraj vs Ganapati And Anr on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117769933/
4 (iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the interest accrued on it.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7442 HC-KAR (v) The respondent-insurance company is at liberty to recover the said amount on the owner of the vehicle by due process of law.
